section_summary: This section covers U.S. State Department and Far Eastern Commission documentation from March to May 1948 concerning economic rehabilitation and foreign aid for Japan, Korea, and the Ryukyu Islands. It contains diplomatic despatches reporting the views of Japanese political leaders on American aid and economic self-support, interdepartmental correspondence coordinating State and Army Department support for a $275 million rehabilitation appropriation request, and draft statements defending American occupation economic initiatives before the Far Eastern Commission against Soviet objections.

subfiles.about: Concluding portion of a despatch enclosure reporting views of Bank of Japan Governor Ichimada and Matsumoto on political unity, foreign credits, inflation, and communism.
subfiles.summary: Governor Ichimada urges foreign credits, balanced budgets, and tax measures, while Matsumoto notes the pervasive influence of Marxism among Japanese leaders.
subfiles.title: Enclosure No. 1 to Tokyo Despatch No. 204: Comments of Governor Ichimada and Mr. Matsumoto on Japanese Economic and Political Situation

subfiles.about: Transmits comments and views of Japanese leaders regarding U.S. aid for achieving economic self-support, accompanied by four memoranda and statements.
subfiles.summary: Despatch summarizing ten major points on Japanese economic recovery, including the need for U.S. aid, reparations settlement, raw materials, power efficiency, and labor cooperation. Enclosures record conversations with Kurusu Takeo and Tsuru Shigeto, a note from Mizutani Chozaburo, and comments from Suzuki Mosaburo, Matsuoka Komakichi, Matsudaira Tsuneo, and Katayama Tetsu.
subfiles.title: Tokyo Despatch No. 215: Comments of Japanese Leaders Regarding United States Aid for Achieving Self-Support, with Enclosures

subfiles.about: Discusses State Department support for the Army's $275 million rehabilitation appropriation for Japan, Korea, and the Ryukyus, and related enabling legislation.
subfiles.summary: Recommends supporting the Army's $275 million foreign aid figure before the National Advisory Council and resolving legislative conflicts over enabling bills.
subfiles.title: Memorandum from Charles E. Saltzman to Robert A. Lovett: Secretary Royall's Request for Support of Army Department's $275 Million Rehabilitation Program

subfiles.about: Provides estimated foreign financial assistance authorizations for fiscal years 1948 and 1949, including occupied areas relief and reconstruction.
subfiles.summary: Tab A letter detailing projected foreign aid authorization requests totaling over $9.3 billion, including European recovery and occupied area programs.
subfiles.title: Letter to Senator Arthur H. Vandenberg Estimating Foreign Financial Assistance Authorizations (Tab A)

subfiles.about: Transmits the delayed draft reply to Secretary Royall regarding occupied areas rehabilitation funding.
subfiles.summary: Explains delays in replying to Secretary Royall due to evolving circumstances.
subfiles.title: Routing Memorandum from P. P. Claxton, Jr. to Carlisle H. Humelsine regarding Response to Secretary Royall

subfiles.about: Transmits statements listing foreign policy legislation and estimated financial authorizations requested for the current congressional session.
subfiles.summary: Press release containing Counselor Bohlen's letter to House Foreign Affairs Committee Chairman Eaton and detailed schedules of pending foreign policy legislation. It outlines prioritized legislative measures, including the European Recovery Program and Chinese aid, along with estimated appropriations for Japanese-Korean reconstruction, Trieste, and Latin American development.
subfiles.title: Department of State Press Release No. 181: Letter from Charles E. Bohlen to Representative Charles A. Eaton with Statements on Foreign Policy Legislation (Tab B)

subfiles.about: Statistical summary of appropriations, obligations, and expenditures for foreign aid programs across fiscal years 1948 and 1949.
subfiles.summary: Tab C budget table presented by Budget Director Webb showing multi-billion dollar foreign aid estimates.
subfiles.title: Table I: Summary of Budget Estimates for Foreign Aid Programs (Tab C)

subfiles.summary: Duplicate copy of the April 6 memorandum analyzing budget figures and legislative strategy for occupied areas aid.
subfiles.title: Memorandum from Charles E. Saltzman to Robert A. Lovett: Secretary Royall's Request for Support of Army Department's $275 Million Rehabilitation Program (Copy)

subfiles.about: Draft version of memorandum addressing Secretary Royall's request for State Department support of occupied areas rehabilitation funding.
subfiles.summary: Draft version of Saltzman's memorandum proposing coordination with the Army on the $275 million program.
subfiles.title: Draft Memorandum from Charles E. Saltzman to Robert A. Lovett: Secretary Royall's Request for Support of Army Department's $275 Million Rehabilitation Program

subfiles.about: Draft memorandum to the Secretary of State discussing support for the Army's $275 million rehabilitation program and enabling legislation.
subfiles.summary: Proposes informing Secretary Royall of State's qualified support for the rehabilitation program and coordinating on enabling bill amendments.
subfiles.title: Draft Memorandum from Frank G. Wisner to Secretary George C. Marshall regarding Secretary Royall's Request

subfiles.about: Draft revision sheet concerning foreign aid totals and congressional strategy on occupation enabling legislation.

subfiles.title: Draft Page of Memorandum from Charles E. Saltzman regarding Enabling Legislation for Occupied Areas

subfiles.about: Conveys State Department support for the Army's $275 million rehabilitation appropriation request before the NAC and urges agreement on enabling legislation.
subfiles.summary: Affirms State Department support for the $275 million rehabilitation request before the National Advisory Council and proposes introducing an agreed administration bill.
subfiles.title: Letter from Robert A. Lovett to Secretary of the Army Kenneth C. Royall regarding Rehabilitation Appropriation and Enabling Legislation

subfiles.about: Draft page discussing congressional strategy and minor changes in the occupied areas draft bill.
subfiles.summary: Draft page proposing joint congressional strategy for introducing the administration enabling bill.
subfiles.title: Draft Page 2 of Letter from Robert A. Lovett to Kenneth C. Royall

subfiles.about: Earlier draft page on resolving differences over enabling legislation for occupied areas.
subfiles.summary: Draft page addressing coordination between State and Army on congressional presentation of the draft bill.
subfiles.title: Draft Page 2 of Letter from Robert A. Lovett to Kenneth C. Royall

subfiles.about: Draft sheet explaining proposed amendments concerning administration transfer in Germany and contingency aid for Korea.
subfiles.summary: Draft sheet explaining State Department amendments to the occupied areas bill.
subfiles.title: Draft Page of Letter to Kenneth C. Royall regarding Legislative Amendments

subfiles.about: Draft letter assuring State Department support for the $275 million program before NAC and discussing amendments to enabling legislation.
subfiles.summary: Draft letter outlining support for the rehabilitation program and requesting unified presentation of enabling legislation amendments.
subfiles.title: Draft Letter to Kenneth C. Royall regarding Rehabilitation Appropriation and Legislative Amendments

subfiles.about: Draft page regarding congressional handling of the agreed administration enabling bill.
subfiles.summary: Draft page discussing introduction of the unified administration enabling bill in Congress.
subfiles.title: Draft Page 2 of Letter from Robert A. Lovett to Kenneth C. Royall
